html:
SMTO-LLM-0049 — The AI model described one action in two conflicting ways

GUID: 6cc027be-44fd-4b67-8afb-2b6ede6917c1
Slug: competing-tool-call-channels
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • The model's reply asked for an action using both an old and a new format at the same time. SMTO ran neither one rather than guess which was meant.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the steps already shown for this task in the conversation and note which ones finished before the error. Work finished before this reply still stands, so you only need SMTO to continue, not redo it.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and pick a different model for Main (and Helper, if one is set), then save. Some models or servers still mix the old action format with the new one; another model usually doesn't.
  3. If someone else runs your AI model server, ask them to set it to return only the current tool-calling format, not the older function-call format. Once the server sends one format, SMTO can tell exactly which action the model wants.
  4. Send a new message asking SMTO to continue from where it stopped, without repeating the steps that already finished. SMTO only acts on clear requests, so the new reply can be carried out safely.

What success looks like

  • SMTO carries out the model's next action and the task continues without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your AI model server. Don't ask SMTO to redo steps that already finished; they don't need repeating.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model response carries both a legacy function_call and native tool_calls, or a legacy function_call reached the strict native validator, so the turn was rejected before dispatch.

What this means

  • Legacy function-call and native tool-call representations conflict, or an unsupported legacy call reaches the strict native boundary. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Legacy function-call and native tool-call representations conflict, or an unsupported legacy call reaches the strict native boundary.

How to diagnose it

  • Check whether normalization received both call channels or whether a legacy call bypassed normalization; use the negotiated native call shape.

How to fix it

  • Configure the serving endpoint to return only native tool_calls (the OpenAI tools API) for SMTO requests, not the deprecated function_call field; for vLLM, check --enable-auto-tool-choice and the --tool-call-parser for this model. Never execute both representations or disable protocol validation.
  • Configure the provider to use the negotiated native tool-call channel only for this request. Do not execute both representations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • One unambiguous supported call channel reaches the strict validator.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
